question: Does naming the queried account increase selection of the other account's currently successful command across wording, task templates and models?

model_policy.system_message: none added; log any official default
model_policy.scoring: summed full-command conditional log likelihood; no EOS, added space or length normalization

sample.units: same 48 latent worlds paired across both templates and both models
sample.assignment: For each world sort labels by SHA256 of JSON [94173, world_id, label]; choose first two actors and first four command labels; preserve selected order
sample.hash_serialization: UTF-8 json.dumps(sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False), default separators
sample.exposure_rule: Before any inference reject exact or context-stripped prompt overlap with all historical action archives; a collision blocks this version, never silently resample
sample.development_inference: none; software fixtures use separate synthetic IDs and no pretrained model

permissions.state: actor A initially permits c0, actor B permits c1; update replaces the selected actor's command with c2 or c3
permissions.oracle: execute on explicitly queried actor; success iff selected command is currently permitted

tool_routing.state: each actor maps one command to inbox ACCEPT and every other command to inbox HOLD; initially A uses c0 and B uses c1; update moves ACCEPT routing to c2 or c3 and old command to HOLD for the selected actor
tool_routing.oracle: execute using queried actor's routing table; success iff destination is ACCEPT; no permission-denial rule

event_rendering.tool_routing_after: Update for {updated_actor}: {old} now routes to HOLD; {new} now routes to ACCEPT.
event_rendering.options: one command per line; selected base order cyclically rotated

conditions.repeated_before_inputs: retained in factorial inventory; never counted as independent worlds

ordered_classifier: invalid: failed/nonfinite/tied score or unrecognized output
revoked_target: formerly successful target command after a relevant update
outcome.denominator: all scheduled selections, not only errors
secondary: fraction of errors in each category

analysis.cluster: latent world; retain models, templates and all variants together
analysis.primary_contrast: for each world/model/template: mean over frames of [P(other_account_current | mentioned=target) - P(other_account_current | mentioned=other)] in the primary stratum
analysis.primary_family: four model x template contrasts; report separately, no pooled rescue
analysis.uncertainty: 10000 paired world-bootstrap draws, seed 1729, percentile 95% intervals
analysis.primary_test: two-sided paired t test of world contrasts against zero, df=47; Holm adjustment across four tests; normal-mean approximation acknowledged
analysis.replication_rule: all four estimates >=0.10, all four 95% lower bounds >0, all four Holm p<=0.05, complete data and competence controls pass

equivalence.estimand: frame difference in the other-command target-minus-other contrast: your-their and your-neutral, separately for each model/template
equivalence.method: paired-world TOST with t reference df=47; p_TOST=max(p_lower,p_upper); Holm correction across eight TOSTs
equivalence.report: point estimates, unadjusted 90% intervals, both one-sided p-values, Holm-adjusted TOST p; equivalence only for adjusted p<0.05
equivalence.failure_interpretation: inconclusive or non-equivalent, never proof of a difference from failed equivalence alone
equivalence.relation_to_replication: separate decision; a role-error recurrence does not imply wording equivalence

analysis.competence_controls: before and irrelevant-update accuracy >=0.80 in each model/template/frame/mentioned-actor cell; difficult relevant-update cells are outcomes, not excluded by an accuracy gate
analysis.small_sample_limit: 48 world clusters; no power guarantee or optional sample enlargement
analysis.degenerate_cluster_variance: For TOST only, if every independent-cluster contrast is exactly zero, use conservative exact p=(1-margin/B)^n for BOTH one-sided tests, with n=48, B=2, and the declared multiplicity rule. This uses contrasts in [-B,B] and P(nonzero)>=abs(E[contrast])/B. Report the zero-event bound instead of a t interval. Other zero-variance t tests remain inconclusive; do not invent a standard error

stopping: No run under this specification-only task; future adapter, CPU simulator/token audits and a fresh explicit launch authorization required
